title: Popping or backfiring
h1: Why is my car popping or backfiring?
metaDesc: Car popping or backfiring? Answer a few quick questions to see if it's a misfire, exhaust leak or fuel problem, how urgent it is, and what to tell your mechanic.
synonyms: popping noise when letting off gas
intro: A pop or bang from the engine or tailpipe usually means fuel is burning somewhere it shouldn't, either in the intake or in the exhaust. When it happens and what comes with it tells you whether it's a harmless crackle, a leak, or a misfire that can damage expensive parts. Answer the questions below to find the most likely cause and how soon to act.
safety: If the check engine light is flashing, pull over safely and turn off the engine. A severe misfire can overheat the catalytic converter.
If you see smoke or flames from under the car or the tailpipe, pull over, turn off the engine and get away from the car.
If you smell exhaust inside the car, open the windows and stop driving it until it's checked. Exhaust contains carbon monoxide.
If you smell raw fuel, stop the engine and keep sparks and flames away.

q_when.q: When do you hear the popping or backfiring?
q_when.help: A pop from the tailpipe is usually unburned fuel igniting in the exhaust. A pop from under the hood, sometimes with a puff from the air filter area, is a backfire into the intake.

opts.a: Mostly when I let off the gas or coast, a crackle or pop from the tailpipe
When I press the gas or accelerate
At idle or all the time, and the engine feels rough
A pop or cough from under the hood, near the air filter

q_light.q: Is the check engine light on, and how is the engine running?
q_light.help: The check engine light is the amber engine-shaped symbol on the dash. Flashing is much more serious than steady.

opts.a: The check engine light is flashing
The light is on steady, or the engine shakes, stumbles or feels weak
There's a strong fuel smell or black smoke from the tailpipe
No light and it runs fine, but the exhaust is louder or puffing

q_decel.q: Which of these fits your car best?

opts.a: It has an aftermarket exhaust or engine tune, or it's a sporty model that crackles on purpose
The exhaust got louder, puffs or ticks, or I smell exhaust
The check engine light is on, or the engine runs rough
I smell raw fuel or see black smoke
None of these, it's a stock car that just started doing it

result.title: A severe misfire is likely, and it can damage the catalytic converter
result.now: Pull over safely and turn off the engine. Have the car towed or call a mobile mechanic.
if: If the light stops flashing after a restart, don't count on it. The misfire is still there and needs to be checked before you drive any distance.
If you see smoke or smell burning from under the car, get away from the car and call for help.
result.why: A flashing check engine light means one or more cylinders aren't firing. Unburned fuel goes into the exhaust, where it pops and burns inside the catalytic converter. That can overheat and ruin the converter quickly and, in rare cases, start a fire.

causes.name: Failed ignition coil or spark plug
causes.clues: The engine shakes, especially at idle or when accelerating, and the problem came on fairly suddenly.

causes.name: Fuel injector stuck or not spraying
causes.clues: A fuel smell, or the misfire stays on one cylinder after the coil and plug are checked.

causes.name: Mechanical engine problem
causes.clues: A ticking or knocking sound, or a car that has overheated recently.
causes.against: Much less common than an ignition problem.

you: Note whether the engine was shaking and when the light started flashing.

result.title: Most likely a misfire from a worn ignition part
result.now: Have the engine scanned for codes within the next few days. Until then, keep trips short and avoid hard acceleration.
if: If the check engine light starts flashing or the engine shakes hard, pull over and turn it off. Don't keep driving it.
If the spark plugs are past their service interval, mention it. They're a common cause and part of normal maintenance.
result.why: When a cylinder doesn't fire properly, its unburned fuel can ignite later in the exhaust and make a pop. A rough-running engine or a steady check engine light along with popping almost always points to a misfire.

causes.name: Worn spark plugs
causes.clues: The plugs haven't been changed in a long time, or the misfire is worse when accelerating.

causes.name: Weak ignition coil or plug wire
causes.clues: The misfire is worse in damp weather or under load, or it's on one cylinder.

causes.name: Vacuum leak or dirty fuel injector
causes.clues: A rough idle, a hissing sound, or the misfire is spread across several cylinders.

you: Check your maintenance records for the last spark plug change.
Many auto parts stores will read the codes for you.

result.title: A backfire into the intake usually means the engine is running too lean
result.now: Have it checked within the next few days. Avoid hard acceleration until then, since that's when intake backfires happen most.
if: If there's a loud bang and the engine then won't start or runs very badly, don't keep cranking it. The timing belt or chain may have slipped. Have it towed.
If the check engine light starts flashing, pull over and turn off the engine.
result.why: A pop from under the hood means the air-fuel mixture is igniting in the intake instead of the cylinder. That usually happens when there's too much air and not enough fuel, or when the spark is firing at the wrong moment.

causes.name: Vacuum leak
causes.clues: A hissing sound, a rough or high idle, or a cracked hose you can see.

causes.name: Faulty airflow sensor or weak fuel delivery
causes.clues: Hesitation or loss of power when you press the gas, sometimes with a check engine light.

causes.name: Ignition timing problem or slipped timing belt
causes.clues: An older engine, a recent timing belt job, or the backfire came with a sudden drop in power.
causes.against: Less common on modern engines than a lean mixture.

you: With the engine running, listen for hissing around the hoses on top of the engine.
Note whether the check engine light is on.

result.title: Probably an exhaust leak letting air in and causing pops
result.now: Book an exhaust inspection. Mention that it pops when you let off the gas.
if: If you smell exhaust inside the car, or feel drowsy or get a headache while driving, stop driving it until it's fixed.
If the check engine light comes on or the engine starts running rough, get it checked within a few days.
result.why: When you let off the gas, a small amount of unburned fuel goes into the exhaust. If a leak lets fresh air in, that fuel can ignite and pop. A leak usually also makes the exhaust louder or adds a ticking or puffing sound.

causes.name: Leaking exhaust gasket or joint
causes.clues: A ticking or puffing sound, loudest on a cold start, that may quiet down as the engine warms.

causes.name: Rusted or cracked exhaust pipe or muffler
causes.clues: The exhaust is louder than it used to be, or there's visible rust or a hole.

causes.name: Engine running slightly rich
causes.clues: Fuel economy has dropped, or there's a fuel smell at the tailpipe.
causes.against: Less likely if the engine runs smoothly and mileage is normal.

you: With the engine cold and off, look under the car for black soot marks or rust holes along the exhaust.
Listen at the back of the car on a cold start for puffing or ticking.

result.title: The engine is likely getting too much fuel
result.now: Get it checked within the next few days. Keep trips short until then, and don't let it idle for long periods.
if: If the fuel smell is strong or you see fuel dripping, don't drive it. Have it towed.
If the check engine light starts flashing, pull over and turn off the engine.
result.why: Extra fuel that doesn't burn in the engine can ignite in the hot exhaust and pop. It also wastes fuel and can overheat and damage the catalytic converter over time.

causes.name: Leaking or stuck-open fuel injector
causes.clues: A strong fuel smell, a rough idle, or hard starting when warm.

causes.name: Faulty sensor giving the computer wrong readings
causes.clues: A check engine light, poor fuel economy, or black smoke on acceleration.

causes.name: Misfire leaving fuel unburned
causes.clues: The engine shakes or stumbles along with the popping.

you: Look and smell for fuel around the engine and under the car.
Note any change in fuel economy.

result.title: Crackling on deceleration is normal for some sporty exhausts and tunes
result.now: Check whether your model or its tune is known to crackle when you let off the gas. If it's always done this and nothing else has changed, it's likely by design.
if: If the popping is new, getting louder, or comes with a check engine light or rough running, have it checked.
If you smell exhaust inside the car, stop driving it until the exhaust is inspected.
result.why: Some performance cars and aftermarket tunes add a little fuel when you lift off the gas so it burns in the exhaust and crackles. Aftermarket exhausts with less muffling also make normal small pops easier to hear.

causes.name: Factory or aftermarket sport tuning
causes.clues: It has always done it, mainly in a sport mode or after a tune.
causes.against: Less likely if the popping started suddenly on a car that never did it.

causes.name: Less restrictive aftermarket exhaust
causes.clues: It started after an exhaust change.

causes.name: Exhaust leak
causes.clues: A ticking or puffing sound, or a louder exhaust than before.

you: Check whether it only happens in a sport driving mode.
Ask the shop or seller that installed the exhaust or tune whether it's expected.

result.title: Get the engine scanned for codes to narrow it down
result.now: Have the engine scanned within the next few days, and note when the popping happens so you can tell the shop.
if: If the check engine light starts flashing or the engine shakes hard, pull over and turn it off.
If you smell fuel or exhaust inside the car, stop driving it until it's checked.
result.why: Popping can come from a misfire, an exhaust leak or a fuel mixture problem. A code scan and a quick look at the exhaust usually tell them apart in minutes, and catching a misfire early protects the catalytic converter.

causes.name: Misfire
causes.clues: Rough running, shaking, or a check engine light.

causes.name: Exhaust leak
causes.clues: Pops mostly when you let off the gas, with a louder or ticking exhaust.

causes.name: Fuel mixture too rich or too lean
causes.clues: A fuel smell, black smoke, or hesitation when accelerating.

you: Record a short video with sound of the popping. It helps the shop a lot.
